newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline weak, U.S. stocks enough to meet need.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline weak, U.S. stocks enough to meet need.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices dipped sharply on Wednesday, sinking $2-3 a tonne after Tuesday's bearish U.S. inventory news and a report from the API saying U.S. gasoline stocks could meet the most aggressive demand.
Some traders said the market had been expecting a fall in U.S. stocks and said the build had knocked down recent reports of heightened demand for gasoline in the U.S.
However, others said they expected the gasoline build was mainly due to a recent heavy import programme in front of the U.S. driving season and after a recent spell of refinery maintenance.
Most expected demand to pick up again soon as the driving season kicks in although the API said current stock levels were sufficient to meet the most aggressive rise in demand.
"Gasoline imports have been running nearly double last year, and were eventually going to show-up," Sarah Emerson, director of Energy Security Analysts Inc said.

Both spot and paper markets in Europe were hit with prompt Amsterdam/Rotterdam lifting barges trading some $2-3 lower at $190.50 a tonne and May barge swaps pegged back $1-2 at $194/$195. Fob cargo avails were seen out of Scandinavia and the U.K. and prices for these were also pegged $1-2 lower.
The API report showed crude stocks up 2.97 million barrels and gasoline up 3.63 million barrels.
